rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews disguised an insulting wish for death by twisting a greeting so listeners thought they had heard a wish of peace.
rows.anchor: listener would think that they have said the former whereas the matter would be the reverse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording refers to the Jews' delusion that their mischief would go unpunished, which emboldened them to continue it.
rows.anchor: refer to their delusion because of which they continued spreading mischief on not being chastened for it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because no punishment came immediately, they thought rejecting and mocking the Prophet was justified and took the delay as proof his claim was a bluff.
rows.anchor: they reckon that had he been the messenger of God, then they would necessarily have been punished for this conduct

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is a sufficient punishment for them, so the absence of punishment in this world does not matter.
rows.anchor: Hell is sufficient for such people in which they shall necessarily be cast, and what an evil abode it is

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat includes punishment in this world, alluded to in 58:5, and certain punishment in Hell; escape from worldly seizure gives no reassurance.
rows.anchor: not only in this world as is alluded to in verse 5 above and is also mentioned further ahead in the sūrah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not seeing immediate consequences breeds arrogance: people conclude they will never be punished and dismiss preachers' warnings as blackmail.
rows.anchor: When he observes that he is not being punished in this world for his mischief, he becomes assured that he will never be punished

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This world is a trial rather than a place of reward and punishment; if deeds were judged immediately, everyone would choose virtue.
rows.anchor: The real secret of this world is that it is not a place of reward and punishment; it is a place of trial and test

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hereafter's judgment gives the universe meaning and purpose; without it the Creator would be a merry-maker, whereas He is powerful and wise.
rows.anchor: In its absence, the whole universe is rendered meaningless and purposeless and its creator a merry-maker

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Secret conversation is not inherently wrong: social life requires consultation, sometimes confidentially, as a foundation of collective life.
rows.anchor: na jwā (secret conversation) in itself is nothing bad. There are a lot of occasions in our social lives

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Secret consultation for virtue, piety, mutual correction, and reform is a blessing, so Muslims should use it for noble purposes.
rows.anchor: If such a consultation relates to virtue, piety and mutual correction and reformation, then it is a means of blessing

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites' secret talks about sin, transgression, and disobedience to the Prophet are satanic; believers should avoid them.
rows.anchor: secret consultation in which the hypocrites indulge and which relates to sin, transgression and disobedience to the Prophet (sws) is satanic in nature

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should fear God, before whom everyone will be gathered and who knows their secret consultations, as stated earlier.
rows.anchor: keep fearing the God in Whose presence everyone will be gathered, and Who is fully aware of their secret consultations

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan incites hypocrites to secret conversation, and the most he can do is cause sorrow and grief in believers' hearts.
rows.anchor: what best Satan can do is to inflict some sorrow and grief in the hearts of the Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan cannot harm without God's permission, so believers should disregard his provocations, remain firm, and trust God for protection.
rows.anchor: Without the permission of God, he cannot harm people; so the believers should disregard these evil suggestions and provocations of Satan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites whispered in many settings but especially in the Prophet's gatherings, where they could cast aspersions, distress Muslims, and mock or disrespect him.
rows.anchor: they would specially indulge in them in the gatherings of the Prophet (sws) because it was here that they found the greatest opportunities

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites clustered in the Prophet's gatherings and kept others out so they could comment freely; they sometimes stayed after he left to spread mischief or scheme.
rows.anchor: the hypocrites would sit closely together in the form of a group in the gatherings of the Prophet (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These maneuvers called for rules governing the Prophet's gatherings to curb hypocrites' satanic whisperings.
rows.anchor: This situation called for some directives for the gatherings of the Prophet (sws) so that the hypocrites could be stopped from their satanic whisperings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural word for gathering primarily denotes the Prophet's meetings, while extending the etiquette to every gathering so each reflects his gatherings.
rows.anchor: the word is used in its plural form in the verse, the purpose is to guide Muslims to the manners and etiquette they should observe in all gatherings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise, the plural for mosques primarily refers to the Baytullāh in 9:18 but extends the guidance to all mosques, which are subordinate to it.
rows.anchor: since the word occurs in the plural what is intended to be conveyed is that the guidance given relates to all mosques because they are subservient to this great mosque

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the gathering's head asks people to make space, they should obey promptly, sit apart to welcome others, and make it harder for hypocrites to whisper together.
rows.anchor: when the head of the gathering directs the people to sit with spaces between them, then this directive should be obeyed without any hesitation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense of God's making room for them is that He will give them room in Paradise.
rows.anchor: The apparent sense of these words is that the Almighty will create room for them in Paradise

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi gives the deeper application: whoever opens his heart to others will have others' hearts opened to him by God.
rows.anchor: for the person who widens his heart for others, the Almighty widens the hearts of others for him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every deed, public or private and good or evil, has a natural effect; its true manifestation is in the Hereafter, though effects also appear in this world.
rows.anchor: Every deed of a person whether apparent or hidden, good or evil has a natural impact

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order to disperse, whether addressed to a whole gathering or one person, should be accepted without hesitation or a sense of inferiority.
rows.anchor: if in a similar manner, the head of the gathering asks for people to disperse, then this directive too should be obeyed without any hesitation and without any feeling of inferiority

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A collective dispersal should not be taken as disgrace or as the Prophet preferring his comfort over the community's needs or silencing members.
rows.anchor: people should whole-heartedly accept this, and should not think that they have been disgraced or that the Prophet’s personal comfort has been given preference

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone individually asked to move, leave, or yield a seat should obey without complaint; such altruism for the collective system is rewarded with elevation.
rows.anchor: he should obey this directive without complaining. If out of respect for the collective system he behaves in this altruistic manner

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of elevation contrasts with making room: giving up a place may look humiliating, but God makes it a means of elevation for believers.
rows.anchor: Even if this standing up and giving up one’s place may seemingly be humiliating, the Almighty will make this a means of elevation for the believers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about believers among the audience matters because hypocrites would call making room disgraceful; knowledgeable, faithful people who obey wholeheartedly will be rewarded in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: men of knowledge and the faithful who will whole-heartedly obey this directive will be greatly rewarded in the Hereafter by the Almighty

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every sacrifice for faith, the Muslim community, and its collective dignity, and will reward it without needing public publicity.
rows.anchor: In order to become aware of them, He does not need that an advertisement of their deeds and services be published in newspapers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering etiquette applies beyond the Prophet's meetings to all gatherings.
rows.anchor: Though this etiquette has been spelled out for the gatherings of the Prophet (sws), it should be observed in all gatherings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi criticizes Westernized parliaments and councils for factional hostility, secret talk, mockery, and even brawls, while their leaders call police instead of enforcing meeting etiquette.
rows.anchor: our parliaments and council have become more of places of duels. In them, various parties form factions only to defeat one another

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following directive shifts from protecting prophetic meetings from secret talk to shielding the Prophet himself from its perpetrators.
rows.anchor: in the succeeding verses a measure has been suggested in order to shield the person of the Prophet (sws) from the evil of those who indulge in these clandestine talks

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Qur'an condemned their mischief, hypocrites sought lengthy private meetings with the Prophet to claim innocence and blame others for their crimes.
rows.anchor: many hypocrites started having long meetings with the Prophet (sws) to try to prove themselves to be innocent and to incriminate others for their own

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites lacked courage to defend themselves openly and sought private meetings one by one, so restrictions were needed to prevent them wasting the Prophet's time.
rows.anchor: These people did not have the courage to do this in open gatherings and hence each of them would try to meet the Prophet (sws) in private

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This was an emergency restriction; once its purpose was achieved it was abrogated, and the abrogated verses precede the abrogating ones to preserve coherence.
rows.anchor: When the objective was achieved, this directive was abrogated and the abrogated verses were placed right before the abrogating ones

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charity condition came at the height of the whispering campaign to stop hypocrites from wasting the Prophet's time with private meetings and obsequious attempts to shift blame.
rows.anchor: the purpose was to stop the hypocrites from interfering with the cherished time of the Prophet (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the Prophet had set no condition for private meetings, selfish people took undue advantage of his generosity, especially during this period.
rows.anchor: Since the Prophet (sws) had not imposed any condition on meeting in private, such selfish people would take undue advantage of his generosity
